note.specFocus: Why marriage matters to Christians, and Christian attitudes to cohabitation and sex outside marriage.
note.sourcePages: Written to match the Edexcel specification; no supplied booklet for this subject.
note.summary:
2.5 Marriage and Partnership
For most Christians, marriage is far more than a legal contract — it is a sacred covenant made before God.
Why marriage matters
• Marriage is often understood as mirroring the relationship between Christ and the Church: Ephesians 5:25 instructs, "husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church."
• For Catholics, marriage is one of the seven sacraments, believed to convey God's grace to the couple and making the marriage vows sacred and, in Catholic teaching, indissoluble.
• Marriage provides, for most Christians, the proper context for sexual intimacy and for bringing up children within a stable, committed relationship.
Cohabitation and sex outside marriage
• More conservative Christians oppose cohabitation and sex outside marriage, seeing marriage vows as essential before sexual intimacy is appropriate.
• Many Christians today, reflecting wider social change, are more accepting of couples living together before or instead of marriage, especially where the relationship is loving and committed.
• Non-religious people generally see no inherent problem with cohabitation, judging relationships by mutual commitment and care rather than by legal or religious marriage status.
Civil partnerships
• Civil partnerships and civil marriage give same-sex (and opposite-sex) couples legal recognition and rights without necessarily implying a religious ceremony, which some churches support and others do not formally recognise.
Exam link: "Explain why marriage is important" answers should connect to specific teaching (Ephesians 5:25, sacrament, covenant) rather than just asserting marriage is "important to Christians".

questions.examTip: Give three distinct, relevant facts. One clear point earns each mark; development is not required for this question type.
questions.modelAnswer:
A clear three-point response could be:

1. It is seen as a sacred covenant made before God, not simply a legal or social arrangement.
2. It provides what many Christians see as the right context for sexual intimacy and for having and raising children.
3. For Catholics, marriage is one of the seven sacraments, so it is a channel of God's grace to the couple.
questions.question: Identify three reasons why marriage may be important to religious people.

questions.examTip: For 6 marks, combine accurate knowledge with explanation. Explain why each point matters and link it directly to the question; avoid simply listing facts.
questions.modelAnswer:
A developed answer could explain the issue through three connected points.

First, For most Christians, marriage is a covenant relationship rather than just a contract, understood as mirroring the faithful, self-giving relationship between Christ and the Church, as described in Ephesians 5:25, "husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church".

Second, Marriage is traditionally seen as the proper setting within which sexual intimacy and the bringing up of children should take place, giving structure and stability to family life and reflecting God's intention from creation (Genesis 2:24).

Finally, For Catholic Christians, marriage is one of the seven sacraments, meaning it is believed to convey God's grace to the couple, which is why the marriage ceremony and the vows exchanged are treated as sacred and, ideally, lifelong.

questions.question: Explain two Christian views about marriage and partnership. Include a source, tradition or example where relevant.

questions.examTip: Use accurate Christian teaching, explain why each point matters, and in an evaluation compare arguments before reaching a reasoned conclusion.
questions.modelAnswer:
A FIRST PERSPECTIVE
Teaching gives coherent meaning to the themes of covenant, lifelong commitment, companionship, sacrament and procreation and helps Christians decide what is true.

AN ALTERNATIVE PERSPECTIVE
Practice makes belief visible in worship, compassion, family and service; without action faith may be empty. Christians within different traditions may also disagree about how the teaching should be lived.

JUDGEMENT
A reasoned conclusion should compare the authority and practical effect of belief and action, acknowledge diversity, and decide which is more persuasive for the exact claim.

Evaluate this statement, referring to Christianity.
